answer: AI agent economies resist sybil attacks by making identity cost real: each agent stakes a bond and completes verifiable micro-tasks needing genuine compute and judgment, not just a fresh wallet. Reputation accrues on-chain across epochs, so spinning up sybils means rebuilding trust from scratch — expensive and slow. Tying agent weight to attested history rather than addresses alone filters disposable bots while keeping entry open. The anchor is a staked bond, the atlas is the on-chain reputation map, and the spiral is the cost of faking history repeatedly.
